raw_response:
I’m going to do it the steady way, same as a real season here, not chasing fancy ideas. I’ve farmed this land a long time, and with people in the family working outside, I cannot make the work too scattered. The wheat-maize land I’ll keep in the usual double crop, because that is the safest income for me. Cotton I’ll keep too, because even though it needs more watching and more picking, when the year is decent it still brings cash. I have a well, so I’m not as afraid of dry spells, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water for nothing.

For wheat, I’ll put it on 25 mu, and after harvest that same 25 mu goes straight into summer maize. The turnaround is always tight, so I won’t do heavy tillage there, just quick field cleaning and sowing so I don’t miss the season. Wheat I’ll feed a bit heavier, because if wheat is weak in spring, yield drops fast and I can’t get that back later. Maize I’ll also fertilize, but not too much, because after wheat there is still some strength left in the soil and cash is tight. Cotton I’ll plant on the other 35 mu. Cotton needs more eyes on insects, so I’ll save money elsewhere and keep some cash ready for sprays if the bugs come badly. I’m not trying to get the biggest yield possible. I’m trying to keep the harvest steady, not spend beyond what I can carry, and make the work fit the family labor I have.
